title: Even Krishna keeps working
hookLine: people copy what you do, not what you say, and Krishna says even he keeps working for that reason
carry: lokasangraha: what the best do, others follow

lines: PEOPLE WATCH THE ONE IN FRONT.
cards: Spend a day around a small child and you know. They don't do what you tell them. They do what you do.
You say be gentle, then slam the cupboard, and guess which one they learn. Offices, teams, families and whole countries work the same way: people watch the person at the front, and they copy.
Krishna has just told Arjuna to work as an offering. Now he adds a reason Arjuna hadn't thought of. Even if you didn't need to act, other people need you to.

teach.h: JANAKA: A SAGE WHO KEPT HIS THRONE.
teach.b: Krishna begins with the rare person who's already free: someone who delights in the self, is content in the self, has nothing left they need to do. You'd think that person could stop.
But look at King Janaka, Krishna says. Janaka was a ruler well-known for his wisdom, a sage who never left his throne, and he and others like him reached perfection through action.
Then the reason: lokasangraham evapi sampashyan kartum arhasi. Keeping in view the holding-together of the world, you should act.
Lokasangraha: the good of the world, the keeping of people together. Then the well-known line. Yad yad acharati shreshthas tat tad evetaro janah.

teach.h: WHATEVER THE BEST DO, OTHERS DO.
teach.b: Whatever the best person does, others do the same. Whatever standard they set, the world follows.
Here Krishna points at himself. There's nothing in all three worlds I have to do, he says, nothing I lack and need to get. And yet I keep acting.
If I stopped, people everywhere would follow my path, and the worlds would fall apart. So the wise should act as eagerly as the attached do, but unattached, for the good of the world.

And they shouldn't unsettle simpler people who are attached to their work; they should do the work well beside them. One more turn at the end. All actions are carried out by the qualities of nature, the gunas.
Only the one confused by ego thinks, I am the doer: ahankara vimudhatma kartaham iti manyate.

teach.h: LEAD BY DOING, NOT BY TAKING CREDIT.
teach.b: The wise lead by example, and they don't take the credit.

how: Hindu teachers often cite Gita 3.20–3.21, on lokasangraha and on people following the example of the best, when speaking of leadership, parenting and public service, and King Janaka is remembered as the model of a wise person who kept working in the world.

o: a census of a king's people

games.q: what's inside the example — tap the pairs.
p: a sage who kept his throne
the best person, whom others copy
I am the doer: ego's mistake

s: in the Gita, someone truly free can stop acting
Krishna says even the free should act, for the good of the world, like Janaka.
Krishna says he has nothing he must do, yet keeps acting
if he stopped, people everywhere would follow, and the worlds would fall apart.
the wise should shake up simpler people attached to their work
they should work well beside them, not unsettle them.

games.q: you're Krishna. there's nothing in the three worlds you need or lack. what do you do?
o: keep acting, because others follow your path.
withdraw so others learn on their own.
games.why: he keeps acting. if he stopped, he says, people everywhere would follow, and the worlds would fall apart.

practice: Picture the people who see you most, a child, a younger sibling, a coworker, a friend who's struggling, a stranger on your usual bus, and let their faces come one by one.

Ask gently: if they copied exactly what I did yesterday, not what I said, what would they learn? Then pick one small thing you'd be glad for them to copy, and picture yourself doing it in front of them.
If you pray, offer that act to Krishna.

wordCard.voice: Lokasangraha. The good of the world, the holding-together of people. Whatever the best person does, others do the same, so even the free keep working, for the good of the world.

orig.note: Sanskrit: loka, the world, and sangraha, holding together. the good of the world, in Gita 3.20.

carryVoice: Your line: lokasangraha, what the best do, others follow. Even Krishna, with nothing he needs, keeps working. That's day one hundred sixty-nine.
